Then the heat came to Lisbon, and with it, the man across the courtyard.
Every evening at nine, his window opened. Every evening, I pretended not to watch.
He read with his sleeves rolled, a glass of wine catching the last of the light.
Once, he looked up. I didn't look away. Neither did he.
I began to dress for that window. A silk slip the colour of wine. My hair down.
The lamp turned low, so he could see only what I chose.
On the night of the storm, the power failed across the whole street. Candles appeared in w
His was the last. He held it up, like a question.
I crossed the courtyard barefoot, rain on my shoulders, my heart louder than the thunder.
"I wondered when you'd come," he said. "So did I," I told him.
For three summers I had been careful. That night, I was honest.
I told him exactly what I wanted, and I watched it land in his eyes. Not surprise. Relief.
His hand found the small of my back. Mine found the buttons of his shirt, slowly, one at a
The candle burned down. The rain didn't stop until morning.

places.name: The tiled courtyard
places.design: A small, square, private courtyard paved with worn, irregular terracotta tiles and surrounded by three-storey residential buildings with tall windows and painted shutters. At dusk, the last orange sunlight rakes across it. *At night, it is plunged into near-total darkness*, lit only by the glow from the few visible windows and, during a heavy rainstorm, the carried candles. The framing windows are the real set pieces: Tomás's (open blue shutters) and Inés's (open, no shutters). Weather shifts from dry dusk to a heavy, sound-muffling rain at night.

places.name: Tomás's apartment
places.design: A modest, lived-in 19th-century Lisbon apartment. Monochromatic base of faded white plaster and dark wood floor. Primary colours are in the details: blue shutters on the window, an ochre blanket, a worn Persian rug. Key permanent elements: a tall wooden window frame with deep sill, a heavy timber door, an old armchair, a low bedside table. Nightlight comes solely from one or two flickering, warm-toned candles held or placed in the room. At dawn, cold blue-grey light filters through rain-streaked glass.

places.name: Inés's apartment
places.design: A slightly austere apartment in an old building. Off-white plaster walls, dark wood flooring. Furniture is sparse: a simple wooden wardrobe, a standing lamp with a cream fabric shade (warm, low, single source of light), a small wooden-framed mirror. The colour accent is the wine-red silk of the slip dress. The tall window has no curtains, only inward-opening blue shutters. The weather is dry dusk turning to night.
